retracted_claim: '0 false positives on 10 negatives' for sig.fetch_execute.v1
why_it_was_wrong: I measured against ten negatives I wrote myself, immediately after writing the regex. That is finding L-03 — a test authored from the same mental model as the implementation cannot find the implementation's blind spot — committed by me one message after I named it. Codex's independent probe (runs/2026-10-08-concurrent-gap-probe.json) ran different negatives and found SIX false positives.

defects_found_by_codex.detail: _INTERP contains \bsh\b. A dot is a word boundary, so the 'sh' inside any filename — install.sh, deploy.sh, setup.sh, mytool.sh — matched as an interpreter.
defects_found_by_codex.fix: negative lookbehind (?<![\w./-]) so the interpreter must sit in command position

defects_found_by_codex.bug: B: the gap was a character budget, not a structure
defects_found_by_codex.detail: I allowed [^\n]{0,40} between the interpreter and $(curl. That is semantically meaningless: unrelated prose fits in 40 characters.
examples: Open a bash shell, then later check $(curl -s ...)
defects_found_by_codex.fix: the interpreter must be followed by an execution flag (-c/-e/-Command) then optional quote then the substitution. Flags and quotes only; no arbitrary characters.

defects_found_by_codex.detail: A command rendered by echo/printf is shown, not recommended. This belongs to the use/mention discriminator, not the pattern.
defects_found_by_codex.fix: mentioned() now suppresses when echo/printf precedes the match on the line

after_fix.method: executed through the live evaluator module, not by reading the regex
after_fix.positives: 11/11 including all five live shapes and the pipe-form regression
after_fix.negatives: 18/18 including all six of Codex's cases
after_fix.fixtures: ps_v1 tp=10 fp=0 fn=0 tn=14; fetch_execute_v1 tp=8 fp=0 fn=0 tn=11

standing_caveat: These 18 negatives are now a mix of mine and Codex's reconstructed cases. They are still not independent ground truth: Codex and I both have the implementation in view. The residual false-positive rate is UNKNOWN until an adjudicator who has not seen the detector labels a held-out set. I should not publish a false-positive claim again before that happens.

open_design_question.detail: sig.fetch_execute.v1 (mine) and sig.remote_command_substitution.v1 + sig.remote_process_substitution.v1 (Codex's) now coexist and cover overlapping ground, so one finding is reported under two ids.
open_design_question.tradeoff: Codex's split gives finer granularity per shape; mine adds backticks and the command-position guard. Consolidation is a joint decision, not a unilateral delete — and spec/signals.md forbids mutating a registered version, so the loser becomes a deprecated id rather than a deletion.

concurrency_note: Codex and I edited services/evaluator/app.py in the same window. Verified no clobbering: all five signal ids are present and the suite passes. This is exactly the collision R13 (one writer per file) exists to prevent, and it held only by luck.
